use_case: Build fault-tolerant, long-running business workflows and distributed applications with durable execution.
Coordinate unreliable external services, users, devices, microservices, and infrastructure operations with retries and recovery.
Implement order processing, payments, provisioning, cloud automation, ML training pipelines, and other processes that must complete despite crashes.
pros: Very strong durability model: workflow state and event history allow execution to recover, replay, pause, and continue after failures.
Excellent fit for distributed systems, microservices coordination, long-running business processes, retries, timeouts, and compensation logic.
Polyglot SDK ecosystem lets teams write workflow and activity code in general-purpose languages rather than YAML-only orchestration.
Can be self-hosted or used through Temporal Cloud; application workers remain in the team's own infrastructure.
cons: Higher conceptual and operational complexity than simpler Python-first orchestrators: workflows, activities, workers, task queues, histories, and determinism rules must be understood.
Requires a Temporal service plus workers, so setup is heavier for small scripts or simple scheduled data jobs.
Workflow code must follow deterministic execution constraints, which can surprise teams new to replay-based systems.
Not specifically designed around LLM agent graphs or prompt/tool evaluation workflows.
